clue.text: Novel arrangement for Cindy and us with a little shiner about

indicators.note: the small star goes about, that is around, the rearranged letters

parts.note: a starlet is a little star, and stars shine

indicators.note: an arrangement of the names Cindy and us puts their letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone shuffles a story for Cindy and friends, featuring a minor celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' shuffles the two names, and 'about' puts the starlet round them, split after its first two letters. Conan Doyle's first Sherlock Holmes novel results.
explanation.definitionFit: The first Sherlock Holmes story by Arthur Conan Doyle is a full-length work of fiction.

clue.text: Novel Nato leader missing about to spend time with home help turning up

indicators.note: the shortened alliance name goes about, around, the pieces for spend and time
the alliance name loses its first letter, its leader

parts.note: to pass time is to spend it
an age is a period of time
in means at home

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reads the word for help from bottom to top

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: With the alliance's chief gone, someone is about to while away time while their domestic help arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader missing' takes the alliance's first letter off, and 'about' wraps the rest round the spend-time pair; 'turning up' flips the help word in this down clue. 'home help' looks like one cleaner but splits in two.
explanation.definitionFit: E. M. Forster's novel about British India is a classic work of fiction.

clue.text: Buffoon's vessel, labeled "unkind", not starting

definitions.note: read as buffoon is, so the definition is the noun buffoon

parts.note: a pan is a cooking vessel
something labeled carries a tag, a label

indicators.note: the word for unkind loses its first letter

parts.note: cruel means unkind

explanation.surface: A jester's pot bears a label calling him harsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not starting' drops the C of CRUEL. The step from 'labeled' to TAG, with a tag, is a loose one. The 's is read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabelais's giant is a coarse comic figure, the namesake of gross buffoonery, so a clownish character.

clue.text: Be punctilious having to get back for the fish

indicators.note: the answer must still get the word back added to make the fish, so that word is missing from it

parts.note: the stickleback is a small spiny fish
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fussy person insists on getting a fish returned.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer plus BACK makes the fish, so the fish less BACK is the answer. 'get back' looks like a return, but BACK is just a word to add.
explanation.definitionFit: To stickle is to insist fussily on small points of rule or etiquette.

clue.text: God mostly at home

indicators.note: most of the word God is kept, losing one letter, here the first

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: A deity who rarely goes out.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue works twice. Usually 'mostly' drops a last letter; here it drops the first, which the blog calls not Ximenean but typically Araucarian.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief god of Norse mythology, ruler of Asgard, is a deity.

clue.text: Novel part of the the Venus de Milo's autobiography?

definitions.text: Novel part of the the Venus de Milo's autobiography?

parts.words: Novel part of the the Venus de Milo's autobiography?
parts.note: the armless statue's memoir would naturally describe the moment she lost her limbs, which is also the title of a Hemingway novel

explanation.walkthrough: The Venus de Milo is the famous Greek statue with no arms; her life story would include saying goodbye to them. The printed 'the the' is a slip.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemingway's First World War novel is a work of fiction, and its title fits the armless statue's story.

clue.text: Novel cosmetic unfinished amid composer and port not started

indicators.note: the cut-down cosmetic sits amid the other letters
the composer and the port each lose their first letter

parts.note: Bach, the German composer
Bristol is an English port city

indicators.note: the cosmetic loses its last letter

parts.note: mascara is make-up for the eyelashes

explanation.surface: Half-applied make-up sits between a composer and a city in an odd scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not started' beheads the composer and the port, 'unfinished' docks the cosmetic, and 'amid' sets it inside the trimmed port. Dickens's festive ghost story results.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's festive ghost story about Scrooge is a short work of fiction.

clue.text: Stick with scheme to be in funny hats

indicators.note: the scheme is to be put in the jumbled letters
funny suggests the letters of hats are made odd, rearranged

parts.note: a plan is a scheme

explanation.surface: A walking stick is part of a plan involving comic headgear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny' rearranges the headgear, and 'to be in' places the scheme inside that jumble after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashplant is a walking stick cut from an ash sapling.

clue.text: Wrong to change sides?

definitions.meaning: a wrong as a noun, a flaw or fault
to desert one's side for the opposing one

explanation.definitionFit: A defect is a fault, and to defect is to desert to the other side.

clue.text: Reddish colour with or without some extremes

definitions.text: Reddish colour with or without some extremes

indicators.note: the colour takes extra letters within it

parts.note: rust is a reddish-brown colour

indicators.note: the first and last letters of the word some

explanation.surface: A shade of red that stays red whether trimmed or not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremes' takes the first and last of 'some', and 'with' sets them inside. The whole clue is the definition: the colour is a reddish one with those two letters or without them.
explanation.definitionFit: Russet is a reddish-brown shade, as on some apples and autumn leaves.

clue.text: Carry on moving, keeping time the other way

indicators.note: the jumbled letters keep, that is hold, the time letter
the letters of carry on are moving into a new order

explanation.surface: Keep going, even while turning back the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges the first two words, and 'keeping' holds the time letter inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Contrary means opposite in direction or position, going against.

clue.text: Stars of fairly radical sort among dark materials

indicators.note: the word is part of fairly radical, drawn from those words

explanation.surface: A somewhat extreme character from a fantasy trilogy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort among dark materials' adds that Lyra is the heroine of Philip Pullman's His Dark Materials trilogy, a radical sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyra is a northern constellation, a group of stars containing Vega.

clue.text: First half of Orwell's girl's opera location

annotationWithheld.clue: First half of Orwell's girl's opera location

clue.text: Capable of being rooted out, making tip be "relax!"

indicators.note: making signals the letters of the following words are made into something new

explanation.surface: An instruction to tell a tip to relax, so that it can be removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' rearranges TIP BE RELAX.
explanation.definitionFit: To extirpate is to root out completely, so this adjective means capable of eradication.

clue.text: Keep sun off hop?

indicators.note: off suggests the letters of keep sun are spoiled, out of order

explanation.surface: Hopping about keeps the sun from shining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges KEEP SUN. A hop is an informal dance, which a British knees-up, a lively party, is.
explanation.definitionFit: A hop is an informal dance, and a knees-up is a lively party with dancing.

clue.text: Astronomer royal: the French setter's on the next page

parts.note: PTO, please turn over, tells a reader the text continues on the next page
le is French for the
the setter's means my, the crossword-writer referring to themselves

explanation.surface: The royal astronomer's appointment is announced overleaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Astronomer royal' looks like the official title; it is two definitions run together: Ptolemy the astronomer and the Ptolemies, the royal house of Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: Ptolemy was the Alexandrian astronomer, and Ptolemy was also the name of Egyptian kings.

clue.text: Well said between physician and self

parts.note: in the proverb Physician, ... self, the words spoken between physician and self are ...

explanation.surface: A doctor's advice to look after themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb from Luke's Gospel is 'Physician, heal thyself'; the words that come between 'physician' and 'self' join into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Well, in the sense of in good health, is a synonym.

clue.text: Beginning and ending in September, hot amid less hot — yes, inside — so it does

definitions.text: Beginning and ending in September, hot amid less hot — yes, inside — so it does

indicators.note: the following pieces go inside the outer letters of the month
the first and last letters of the month name
the letter for hot sits amid the word for less hot

parts.note: cool means less than hot
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps
yea is an old word for yes

explanation.surface: A remark that something starts and finishes in September amid shifting temperatures, and so it does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beginning and ending in' takes the month's first and last letters; 'amid' puts the hot letter into the less-hot word, and 'inside' fills the month's ends. The British academic year starts in September.
explanation.definitionFit: The academic year in Britain runs from September, so the clue describes its own answer.

clue.text: See 21
Unjustified, being worn out with Gulf problem

indicators.note: a problem with the letters of worn and Gulf means they are jumbled

explanation.surface: Tired of the Gulf crisis, deemed unwarranted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problem' rearranges WORN and GULF.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrongful means unfair or unlawful, lacking justification.

clue.text: Very little idea of wanting a match

parts.note: fain is an old word meaning eager, wanting
a test is an international match in cricket or rugby

explanation.surface: Hardly any notion of wanting a game.
explanation.walkthrough: As in 'I haven't the faintest', the answer alone stands for the slightest idea.
explanation.definitionFit: The faintest is the slightest notion, as in not having the faintest.

clue.text: Embodiment of one 11 to a sailor

parts.note: a means one
11 across is contrary; contrary to is versus, abbreviated V
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: An image of a single fellow facing up to a seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: The number 11 stands for that answer, CONTRARY; 'contrary to' means against, versus, abbreviated V.
explanation.definitionFit: An avatar is an incarnation or embodiment of a deity or idea.

clue.text: Renaissance patrons of Sir Thomas Browne

definitions.meaning: the Florentine banking family who sponsored artists
Browne, a physician, wrote Religio ..., and the Latin word there means of a doctor

explanation.definitionFit: The Florentine family were patrons of the arts, and the Latin genitive means of a physician, as Browne was.

clue.text: Semicircular object of prince and senior soldier in the nude?

parts.note: Hal is Prince Henry in Shakespeare's Henry IV plays
FM stands for field marshal, the top army rank
with 0, nothing, ON, that is wearing nothing

explanation.surface: A shape belonging to a prince and a general who has stripped off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the nude' reads as 0 ON, nothing on. The '?' hints at mooning, showing a bare bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-moon is a shape like half a disc, as on a fingernail or a pair of reading glasses.
